column2: It was a servant who told you, eyes on the floor, and then a second one, and then the whole hall seemed to know. [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] has been slipping away at night, and the one waiting in the dark is [lover_target.GetTitledFirstName].\n\nThe chapel bell has not yet rung for vespers. There is time to settle this before supper.
I will have it out with [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName].
I will have it out with [lover_target.GetFirstName].
Your spouse is confronted about the affair
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has found out about your lover. [From.GetSheHeCap] stands in the doorway of your chamber, white with anger, and demands that you end it tonight.
I will not give them up. Not for you, not for anyone.
You are right. It is over.
The lover is confronted

[From.GetTitledFirstName] corners you in the gallery, voice low and shaking. [From.GetSheHeCap] knows what you have been doing with [From.Spouse.GetFirstName], and [From.GetSheHe] wants it stopped. Now.
Your [From.Spouse.GetHusbandWife] comes to me of [From.Spouse.GetHerHis] own free will.
Very well. I will leave [From.Spouse.GetHerHim] be.
Say that again and I will claw your eyes out.
Meddle in my affairs and you will regret it.
Your rival may hurt you
Your rival may poison you

The blow came out of nowhere, in a dark corridor of your own castle. By the time the guards arrived [From.GetFirstName] was gone, and you were on the flagstones in a pool of your own blood. You do not need the physicians to tell you who sent this message.

For weeks now you have been weak and shaking, food tastes of ash and your hair comes out in the comb. The physicians speak of ill humours. You know better. [From.GetFirstName] has been seen in the kitchens.
Curse [From.GetHerHim]!
Everyone at court seems to know but you. [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] has taken a lover, and does not trouble to hide it. The servants whisper, the courtiers smirk, and your own honour is the price.
Bring [Root.Spouse.GetHerHim] to me.
[lover_target.GetFirstName] has taken to [lover_target.GetHerHis] bed with a fever, and the physicians shake their heads. [lover_target.GetSheHeCap] asks for you in [lover_target.GetHerHis] sleep.
I will nurse [lover_target.GetHerHim] myself.
Send for the best physician gold can buy.
A sickbed is no place for love. It is over.
[lover_target.GetFirstName] lies wounded, the bandages already dark again. The barber-surgeon says the wound may fester, and that a gentle hand at the bedside helps more than people think.
I will sit by [lover_target.GetHerHim] day and night.
Fetch a surgeon who knows the work.
I cannot bear to see [lover_target.GetHerHim] like this. It is over.

You cannot stop thinking about [lover_crush.GetFirstName]. At table you watch [lover_crush.GetHerHim] across the hall, in the courtyard you find reasons to be where [lover_crush.GetSheHe] is, and at night you lie awake rehearsing what you would say.\n\nPerhaps it is time to say it.
I will tell [lover_crush.GetHerHim] how I feel.
[lover_crush.GetSheHeCap] is not that pretty anyway.
Your feelings are returned
Your feelings are scorned
[From.GetFirstName] has caught you alone by the well, red to the ears, and blurted out that [From.GetSheHe] loves you.
I... I feel the same.
You? Do not make me laugh.
You are in love
[From.GetFirstName] took your hand and said that [From.GetSheHe] has felt the same for a long time. You walk the rest of the day as if on air.
I am the happiest soul in the world.
You are scorned
[From.GetFirstName] laughed in your face. By supper [From.GetSheHe] had told half the court, and the pages giggle when you pass.
I am a fool, and everyone knows it.
Next time I will not fail.

You and [lover_sweetheart.GetFirstName] were sweethearts once, when you were both too young to know what it meant. Now you are grown, and when your eyes meet across the hall the old warmth is still there.
What we had was love. It still is.
It was a thing of our youth, nothing more.
You become lovers
[From.GetFirstName] found you on the battlements at dusk and said that [From.GetSheHe] never stopped loving you. You did not let [From.GetHerHim] finish.
My love.
It was only a memory
[From.GetFirstName] took you aside, kind but firm. What you had as children was sweet, [From.GetSheHe] says, but it belongs to the past.
Yes. It was a sweet time.
But I loved you. I still do.

Your [lover_teen.GetSonDaughter] [lover_teen.GetFirstName] has taken to mooning about the courtyard and sighing at supper. It takes the steward to tell you why: [lover_teen.GetSheHe] is sweet on one of the courtiers.
How sweet. Let the young ones have their fun.
It will pass. These things always do.
I will not have it. Keep them apart.
Your wife has grown cold to you, or you to her. Your bed is empty and your nights long. And there is [lover_target.GetFirstName], who laughs at your jokes and lingers when the hall empties.
I am the lord here. I will have her, and let the court talk.
A quiet word, a back stair. No one need know.
No. It would be a sin against the gods and my wife.
Your maid would not meet your eyes all morning, until you made her tell you. Your husband has taken a mistress into his bed, and the whole castle knows it.
He will answer to me for this.
You make advances to the lady

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has made it plain what [From.GetSheHe] wants from you: a gift left on your pillow, a note in [From.GetHerHis] own hand, an invitation to [From.GetHerHis] chambers after the feast.
I accept.
I am not some tavern wench, my lord.
She accepts
[From.GetFirstName] came to your chambers after the feast, as you asked.
Excellent.
She scorns you
[From.GetFirstName] sent your gift back with a curt note, and has made sure the ladies of the court have read it.
Curse her. I will not lower myself again.
Your wife confronts you
[From.GetFirstName] storms into your solar, past the guards, and screams at you until the windows ring. She knows everything, and she will not forgive it.
Woman, hold your tongue.

After all these years, something has changed. When [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] enters the room your heart quickens, and you catch yourself smiling at nothing. It seems you have fallen in love with your own [Root.Spouse.GetHusbandWife].
I am a lucky soul. I will tell [Root.Spouse.GetHerHim] tonight.
Love is a weakness. I will not give in to it.
A whole week with nothing to do. [lover_target.GetFirstName] has hinted, more than once, that [lover_target.GetSheHe] would like to see more of you.
We will ride to the hunting lodge, just the two of us.
I will throw a feast in [lover_target.GetHerHis] honour.
I would rather go drinking with my friends.

[lover_target.GetFirstName] is in a sulk. You never take [lover_target.GetHerHim] anywhere, [lover_target.GetSheHe] complains, never give [lover_target.GetHerHim] anything, never show the court what [lover_target.GetSheHe] means to you.
Then let the whole realm see it. A great feast!
Come hunting with me tomorrow.
You will get exactly what you deserve. Nothing.

There are hard days, and there have been many lately. But [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] is always there, a hand on your shoulder, a cup of wine, a word that makes the weight easier to carry. You have been blessed in your marriage.
I do not know what I would do without [Root.Spouse.GetHerHim].
The gods smile on us.
Together we can bear anything.
You want to surprise [lover_target.GetFirstName] with something, a token of what [lover_target.GetSheHe] means to you.
I will write [lover_target.GetHerHim] a poem.
A flower from the castle garden.
A precious trinket from the merchants of Marienburg.
The affair ends
The fire has gone out. Where once you counted the hours until you could be alone with your lover, now you find excuses to stay away. It is time to end it.
It was good while it lasted.
Your lover leaves you
[From.GetFirstName] has told you, plainly and without tears, that it is over between you.
So be it.
You love [lover_target.GetFirstName] with all your heart, and she is another man's wife. Every time you see them together at court it is a knife between your ribs.
I will pour my pain into verse.
Wine. A great deal of wine.
I will pray for the strength to bear it.
I must let her go.
Stolen hours, back stairs, the fear of footsteps in the corridor. Loving [lover_target.GetFirstName] means loving another man's wife, and it is wearing you down.
And so it ends.
Maybe it can still work. A little longer.
I will make it work, whatever it costs me.
A spouse at home, a lover in the shadows, and lies to keep them apart. The double life is taking its toll: you sleep badly, eat little and jump at every knock on the door.
Enough. I will end every affair and settle down.
I will just have to try harder.
Why hide it? I do not care what my spouse thinks.
Your spouse finds out about the affair
You had planned the night with [lover_target.GetFirstName] for weeks. Now [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] says she wants you at her side tonight, of all nights.
I will go to [lover_target.GetFirstName] anyway.
A ball! And [lover_target.GetFirstName] shall be invited.
I will stay with my wife.
Your wife meets your mistress
At the ball you saw how your husband looked at his guest, and how she looked back. The whole hall saw it.
I will never forgive him.
Your wife hates you
Since the ball [From.GetFirstName] will not speak to you, will not eat with you, and has had her things moved to the far tower.
Women.

[Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] has gone on pilgrimage, to spend a season among the priestesses at a shrine of Shallya. The castle is quiet, the nights are long, and [lover_target.GetFirstName] is close at hand.
Let us make the most of it.
Yes, but discreetly. Servants talk.
We should remain only friends.
I will use the time to work.
Your liege would never let you marry. So the two of you rode out before dawn, found a hedge priest who asked no questions, and were wed before noon.
We are free!
Your liege hears of the elopement
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has run off with [From.Spouse.GetFirstName] and married [From.Spouse.GetHerHim] in secret, without your leave. The court waits to see what you will do.
They have defied me. They will be punished.
Let them be. Young love is no crime.
The pair are imprisoned
[From.GetTitledFirstName] did not take your marriage well. The guards came at dawn, and now you have a cell for a bridal chamber.
At least we are together. Somewhere.
The pair are banished
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has banished you and your new spouse from the court. You have until sundown to be gone.
We will make our own way.
You and [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] love each other dearly, and yet the nursery stays empty. The midwives have nothing to say that you have not heard before.
We will pray for a child.
Then we will try every night until it works.
Another day of cold looks and colder words from [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName]. Only [lover_target.GetFirstName] understands you, only in her arms can you forget.
We will go away to a quiet manor, the two of us.
She will come to me here at the castle.
I do not need comforting.
Your wife finds out
A note in a hand you know well: your mistress is with child, and the child is yours.
Well, well.
You came back early from the chapel and found another woman in your own chambers, with your husband. In your own bed.
I will make him pay for this!
You have found out about [From.GetFirstName]'s affair. All those nights away, all those lies. You will never trust [From.GetHerHim] again.
From this day you are my enemy.
[Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] is waiting up when you come in, a candle burning low. Where do you go at night, [Root.Spouse.GetSheHe] asks. Whom do you see.
That is none of your business.
Matters of the realm. Important work.
Nothing to worry about, my dear. I swear it.
You are right. I will stay home more.
[lover_target.GetFirstName] is in tears. You love [Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] more, [lover_target.GetSheHe] says, you always will, and [lover_target.GetSheHe] is only your plaything.
An expensive gift will dry those tears.
We will go away together for a while.
There, there. You know I love you.
You are right.
[Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] has had enough. At the high table, in front of the whole court, [Root.Spouse.GetSheHe] told everyone about your lover, and gave the details.
Lies! I have no lover, and never will.
And? Half this court has a lover.

Your wife does not even trouble to hide her lover any more. The lover sits beside her at the feasts, and she leaves with them when the candles burn low, and the court watches you to see what you will do.
I will bear it.
Throw the lover in the dungeon.
Throw her in the dungeon.
Throw them both in the dungeon!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has found out about you and his wife. The guards dragged you from her chambers to the dungeon.
It was worth it.
Your husband [From.GetTitledFirstName] has had enough of your lover, and of you. The guards have taken you to the dungeon.
Monster!

Months in the field, mud and smoke and the screams of the wounded. At night you lie in your tent and think of your lover, far away. There are camp followers enough to make a soldier forget, if [Root.GetSheHe] wanted to.
I will stay faithful.
I will pray for strength.
A soldier must find comfort where [Root.GetSheHe] can.
You may fall in love with your own spouse
